value.note: The datasheet DOES have an authoritative table — it is called 'Recommended Power Supply Characteristics' (Table 5-2, §5.2, p.52), not 'Recommended Operating Conditions'. Its minimum column reads '2.3/3.0' with footnote 2 resolving which applies: 3.0 V for chips carrying 3.3 V flash or PSRAM in-package, 2.3 V for chips without. So the two premises are genuinely different chip variants, NOT disagreeing sources. Variants with in-package flash/PSRAM: ESP32-U4WDH (4 MB flash), ESP32-D0WDR2-V3 and ESP32-D0WDRH2-V3 (2 MB PSRAM). Variants without: ESP32-D0WD, ESP32-D0WD-V3, ESP32-D0WDQ6, ESP32-D0WDQ6-V3 (Table 1-1, p.11). on_unknown is 'strictest' (3.0 V floor) because the variant is often not declared in a requirement and the tighter floor is the safe default. Absolute maximum for all supply pins is 3.6 V (Table 5-1, p.52).

freq_vs_supply.reason: There is no voltage-derated frequency table for the ESP32: the CPU clock comes from the PLL fed by the fixed 40 MHz crystal, and the datasheet states no maximum-frequency-versus-supply relationship (contrast the AVR speed grades). The crystal itself is a single mandated value, captured in clock_external.

value.note: The external crystal clock source is COMPULSORY and the ESP32 firmware only supports a 40 MHz crystal; accuracy must be within +/-10 ppm. A series inductor is required on the XTAL_P clock trace (0 ohm initially, adjusted after testing).

source.doc: ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines (Espressif, Release master)

value.note: Complete GND plane under RF, crystal and chip. The crystal must sit at least 2.7 mm from the clock pin, with high-density ground via stitching around the clock trace. No vias on the clock input/output traces. Series components go on the chip side; matching capacitors sit at the two sides of the crystal at the end of the clock trace so their ground pads are close to the crystal's. Do not route any signal trace under the crystal, keep power-trace vias as far from the clock trace as possible, and keep magnetic components away.

source.doc: ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines (Espressif, Release master)

cap.note: At least 10 uF, together with an ESD protection diode, where the external supply enters the PCB.

source.doc: ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines (Espressif, Release master)

cap.note: When the chip power entrance is not near VDD3P3, add a 10 uF capacitor at BOTH the chip power entrance and VDD3P3; if they are close the two can be merged into one. Add an LC circuit on the VDD3P3 rail to suppress high-frequency harmonics, with the inductor rated 500 mA or above.

value.per_supply_pair_note: Place appropriate decoupling capacitors at the rest of the power pins; ground vias should be added close to each capacitor's ground pad to ensure a short return path (HW guidelines §1.4.2, p.19, PDF p.23). No capacitance is stated for those remaining pins, so no value is asserted.

bulk.text: Branch the power in a star layout after the entrance capacitor to reduce pin-to-pin coupling; the guidelines give no additional bulk value beyond the 10 uF entrance capacitor.

source.doc: ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines (Espressif, Release master)

value.placement_note: Ground pads of the chip and of the surrounding components must make full contact with the ground copper pour rather than being connected through traces (HW guidelines §1.4.2, p.19, PDF p.23). No numeric distance is stated.

value.details: CHIP_PU (pin 9) enables the chip when high and resets it when low. The datasheet states explicitly: 'Do not leave the CHIP_PU pin floating' (DS Table 2-1, p.14). When the ESP32 runs from a 3.3 V system supply the rails need time to stabilise before CHIP_PU is pulled up, so CHIP_PU must be asserted high AFTER the 3.3 V rail is stable — which is why an RC delay on CHIP_PU is part of the reference design (HW guidelines §1.3.3 Chip Power-up and Reset Timing, p.7, PDF p.10). Unlike the STM32 and AVR this is a required external network rather than an optional one.
